comment: S15 (#486): where src/commands/scan.js and src/lib/clean.js intentionally answer differently from global/scan.py and clipboard_guard.py. No golden transcript carries one of these: each is a path the Python original crashed on or never ran, and each has the named test in test/scan/scan-node.test.js. residuals: what is the same by construction but not measured, named so it is not discovered later (#470, convention 3).

differences.what: git is not on PATH, in a mode that needs git.
differences.why: The original called git through subprocess.run, which raised FileNotFoundError: a Python traceback on stderr and exit 1. The port prints 'mhw scan: git was not found on PATH; mhw scan needs it in this mode' and exits 2, the code the original uses for a scan that could not run. --file needs no git in either.
differences.test: without git on PATH a git mode exits 2 and says so; --file needs no git

differences.what: The program's name in its own output: outbound-scan where the original printed mhw scan.
differences.why: #600 took mhw scan out of the CLI (CLI native baseline PRD, section 5: CI calls the engine directly); the scan is .github/scripts/outbound-scan.js now, run by the outbound-scan workflow. Its summary line and its error prefix name the script (outbound-scan: ...), so a reader of the CI log is not sent to a command that no longer exists. Nothing else in either stream changes: the replacement below is applied to the original's transcripts, and every other byte is still compared.
differences.test: the program names itself outbound-scan where mhw scan named itself (#600)

differences.what: No term list and no salt (#589): the original's term-list NOTE lines are gone, and six cases lost their object.
differences.why: #589 removed mhw add-term, the hashed term lists and their salt (CLI native baseline PRD, section 5: third-party terms are judged by the model, never matched against a list). The scan matches patterns only and prints none of the three 'no ... term list could be read' NOTE lines nor the salt NOTE, so every line of the original's stdout matching the 'drop' pattern below is removed before the comparison, and nothing else. Six cases whose whole object was a term list or its salt were removed with their transcripts (note-when-no-term-list, note-when-term-list-empty, note-when-salt-unreadable, synthetic-term-found-without-a-note, note-names-each-private-list, private-list-terms-found), and two declared differences about reading the list and the salt went with them (a non-ASCII list or salt read as unreadable; the salt read from its file, not the Keychain). The corpus (test/clean/clean.test.js) keeps its term cases: clean.js finds no span the original did not, and every recorded span it no longer finds is in a term category (employer-client-term, health, colleague-name); their tokens are still compared exactly.
differences.drop: ^NOTE {4}(no (employer and client|health|colleague-name) term list could be read|the term list's salt)
differences.test: no term list and no salt is read, and no term NOTE is printed (#589)

residuals.why: Every character class, the case-insensitive sets and str.casefold() are pinned to CPython 3.14.6 (Unicode 16.0) in src/lib/clean-unicode.js, so Node's ICU (Unicode 17) changes nothing. NFKD is Node's own: test/clean/unicode.test.js holds it equal to CPython's on every letter, number and mark. The owner's term lists were hashed by whatever Python ran add-term (the Command Line Tools 3.9 has Unicode 13): a term whose normalised form differs between Unicode 13 and 16 would not match, in the Python original exactly as in the port.

The original ran on macOS and Linux only. The port runs on Windows too (the in-process suites run there in CI), prints a changed file's label with / as git does, and reads no Keychain there. The usage line on Windows still says scan is macOS and Linux only: it is pinned by S01's goldens, and the README and AGENTS.md say the same; neither is changed in this slice.

A file is decoded with the replacement character, as the original decoded it, so no lone surrogate reaches the engine from mhw scan. The prompt hook (a later slice) reads JSON, where Python keeps a lone surrogate and JavaScript does too; the corpus has no such case yet.
